title: Boards of laws that name no relation
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt and before ticket B's census. Names are the reduced words of F2 = <x, y>; e(u, v) says names u and v are one place, under transitivity, letter closure e(u, v) -> e(ug, vg) and constancy e(u, v) -> s(u) = s(v); a law is finitely many clause templates over a finite alphabet, and it names no relation when every identity literal relates the same offset of two base names. To be proved: (1) the board states are the subgroups of F2 (Schreier graphs), on B_L the restrictions of right congruences; (2) with no positive identity literal beyond the board axioms, refining an allowed board keeps it allowed, so the tree is allowed whenever any state is; (3) if a law names no relation and allows an infinite board, it allows the tree; (4) every finite board is forced by some law that names no relation; (5) two different boards differ in infinitely many identity distinctions and every place off the tree holds infinitely many names, so off the tree no distinction is flipped by a finite change; (6) for value laws the collapse is allowed iff a constant colouring is iff every board is; (7) identity of indiscernibles at radius r makes boards finite, at radius 1 with one bit boards are the balanced view sets and a plane-like abelian board always comes with a non-abelian one; (8) the commutator rule with an aperiodic Wang-tile law forces exactly the plane.
failure_conditions: A law of ticket B's census with an allowed board whose listed cover is not allowed (target 2).
A law of the census allowing the collapse without allowing every listed board (target 6).
A law of the census with a plane-like abelian board under identity of indiscernibles at radius 1 and no non-abelian one (target 7).
A law that names no relation, with an allowed infinite board and no allowed state on the tree (target 3).
remaining_obligations: Targets 1 to 8, or the record of which fails and why
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of identity distinctions on the names of the free group on two letters; finitary laws over finite alphabets. Identity distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact: equality is not a binding (A51).
